skill.name: subgraph-doctor
skill.description: Diagnose and fix broken Goldsky Subgraphs. Use this skill whenever a user has a subgraph that is failing, stalled, stuck syncing, not indexing, auto-paused, returning errors, or won't deploy. Triggers on: 'subgraph stopped syncing', 'subgraph stuck at block', 'subgraph stalled', 'subgraph failed to deploy', 'indexing error', 'SubgraphSyncingFailure', 'unexpected null in handler', 'no network found', 'deployment already exists', 'subgraph not returning data', 'subgraph endpoint 404', 'reached the subgraph limit', 'rate limited'. Also use when the user names a subgraph alongside a problem. Runs CLI commands directly to check status, read logs, identify root cause, and apply fixes. For building, authoring, deploying, endpoint/tag reference, or optimizing a healthy-but-slow subgraph (e.g. too many eth_calls), use /subgraph-builder instead. For migrating from The Graph, use /subgraph-migrate instead.
skill.summary: Troubleshoot failing Goldsky Subgraphs using filtered logs, indexing metadata, and targeted recovery steps.
skill.author: goldsky-io

security_audit.summary: All 79 static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting or unrelated prose, not shell backtick execution or system reconnaissance. One semantic authorization risk remains: authentication failures lead to advice enabling public endpoint access without explicit approval. No evidence found of credential theft, malicious reconnaissance, or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:153 recommends enabling public endpoint access when queries fail authentication, without requiring explicit approval for the visibility change.
remediation.suggestion: Preserve private access and troubleshoot credentials first. Explain the exposure and obtain explicit approval before enabling a public endpoint.

content.value_statement: Failed deployments and stalled indexing can interrupt applications that depend on Goldsky Subgraphs. This skill guides evidence-based diagnosis, targeted repairs, and support escalation.
actual_capabilities: Check Goldsky authentication and identify the affected subgraph through CLI project and subgraph listings.
Read error-filtered logs and query GraphQL metadata to assess indexing errors and block progress.
Match deployment failures to network, schema, manifest, and version-conflict causes.
Identify common AssemblyScript mapping failures and recommend targeted fixes with an appropriate rewind point.
Guide resume, pause, redeployment, and confirmed last-resort deletion, then verify recovery.
Prepare support escalation details for quota issues, upstream RPC failures, and persistent indexing errors.
limitations: Direct execution requires shell access, an installed Goldsky CLI, and working authentication; otherwise, users must run commands themselves.
New subgraph authoring, migrations, healthy-subgraph optimization, and pipeline diagnosis are delegated to other skills.
Internal infrastructure repairs, quota changes, and higher rate limits require Goldsky support.
Endpoint troubleshooting includes a public-access toggle; do not apply it to private data without explicit authorization.

use_cases.title: Recover Stalled Indexing
use_cases.description: Inspect filtered logs and indexed-block metadata to distinguish mapping errors, transient pauses, and a stale source chain.
use_cases.target_user: Application developers maintaining blockchain data integrations

use_cases.title: Resolve Failed Deployments
use_cases.description: Match deployment errors to incorrect network slugs, incompatible schema definitions, mixed API versions, or existing deployment versions.
use_cases.target_user: Release engineers responsible for Goldsky deployments

use_cases.title: Prepare Support Escalations
use_cases.description: Collect the subgraph identifier, project ID, endpoint, error message, and affected block for operational or upstream RPC incidents.
use_cases.target_user: Support engineers coordinating production incident response

prompt_templates.title: Check a Stalled Subgraph
prompt_templates.prompt: My Goldsky subgraph [name/version] stopped syncing. Check its status, filtered errors, and indexing metadata. Explain the evidence before suggesting changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish the cause of stalled indexing.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Deployment Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Deployment of [name/version] failed with [error message]. Review the relevant manifest or schema and recommend the smallest correction. Do not delete deployments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: diagnose a failed deployment without destructive recovery.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a Mapping Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Subgraph [name/version] reports [handler error] at block [number]. Review entity persistence and null handling. Propose a patch, tests, and rewind point before redeployment.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: connect an indexing error to a mapping repair.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Incident Recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [name/version] using logs, metadata, network checks, and endpoint status. Preserve private access. Request approval before mutations and verify block progress after approved repairs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: coordinate diagnosis and controlled production recovery.

output_examples.input: Illustrative incident: logs show a null entity load after an earlier handler returned without saving.
output: Diagnosis: a later handler attempted to load an entity that was never persisted.
Recommended fix: save the initialized entity on the fallback path and guard later loads.
Recovery: redeploy the corrected mapping and rewind to the first affected block after approval.
Verification: confirm indexing errors clear and the indexed block advances.

output_examples.input: Illustrative incident: deployment reports that the requested network slug was not found.
output: Diagnosis: the manifest specifies an unsupported or incorrect network slug.
Recommended fix: verify the supported-network documentation and confirm the contract exists on the intended chain.
Recovery: correct the manifest and deploy a new version after review.

output_examples.input: Illustrative incident: a private GraphQL endpoint rejects unauthenticated queries.
output: Assessment: an authentication failure does not establish that the endpoint should be public.
Next step: verify the endpoint URL and authorized credentials while preserving private access.
Approval required: confirm the intended audience and exposure before considering a public endpoint.

best_practices: Identify the exact subgraph and collect filtered errors plus indexing metadata before selecting a repair.
Require explicit approval for deletion, rewinds, and endpoint visibility changes; preserve private access during authentication troubleshooting.
Verify recovery with status and metadata checks, and add mapping tests before deploying code changes.
anti_patterns: Guessing the cause without logs or retrieving large unfiltered log streams.
Making a private endpoint public merely to resolve an authentication error.
Deleting deployments or restarting indexing without approval and a clear recovery plan.

faq.question: What problems does this skill diagnose?
faq.answer: It covers existing Goldsky Subgraphs with stalled indexing, mapping errors, deployment failures, endpoint problems, and operational symptoms.

faq.question: Does it execute commands directly?
faq.answer: With Bash available, it runs Goldsky CLI commands directly. Otherwise, it provides one command at a time and interprets pasted output.

faq.question: Does it install or authenticate the CLI?
faq.answer: It checks authentication and refers installation or login problems to the separate auth-setup skill.

faq.question: Can it delete or redeploy a subgraph?
faq.answer: Yes. Its recovery workflow includes redeployment and last-resort deletion, with confirmation required before destructive actions.

faq.question: Should authentication errors be fixed by enabling public access?
faq.answer: No. Preserve private access and verify authorized credentials first. Public access requires explicit approval because it changes who can query data.

faq.question: When does it escalate to Goldsky support?
faq.answer: It escalates quota anomalies, database availability issues, upstream RPC faults, and errors that persist after a verified correction.
